De-link any previously paired devices on both your phone and TV before continuing.

Step 2 — Pair the TV
Tap your TV in the list. Accept the pairing code on both your phone and your TV to confirm the connection.

Step 3 — Confirm the connection
Press the back button on your phone — your TV should now show as connected.
Still not connected? Press on Connect, if you connected more than one TV then Tap on Add / Select TV , choose your paired TV, then it will auto connect.

📝 Please Note
If your TV was paired outside of UFM Pro (e.g. through your phone\'s Bluetooth settings), the remote will not work. Always pair your TV through UFM Pro using the steps above.

Remote Management and FTP servers use unencrypted protocols; SFTP and ADB Terminal connections use secure, encrypted protocols. Cloud storage APIs (Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, S3-compatible) securely communicate with their respective servers over encrypted HTTPS. No other data is transmitted to external servers.

pp_s5_vault_body.text: The Encrypted Vault uses military-grade encryption to protect your files.

tc_features.text:
<item>File Browser — browse, copy, move, rename, and delete files anywhere on your device.</item>
        <item>Encrypted Vault — lock sensitive files behind AES-256-GCM encryption with your own PIN.</item>
        <item>File Server — host an FTP or secure SFTP server directly on your device to share files across your local network.</item>
        <item>Remote Management — manage files over your local Wi-Fi via a built-in HTTP server that supports uploading, downloading, and installing APKs remotely.</item>
        <item>Network Shares — connect to SMB, FTP, and NFS servers on your local network to browse, download, and manage remote files.</item>
        <item>Folder Sync — automatically back up local phone folders to an SMB or FTP network share on a schedule you choose (interval or specific time daily, weekly, or monthly).</item>
        <item>Device Pairing — pair your mobile phone and Android TV over local Wi-Fi to transfer and install files.</item>
        <item>ADB Terminal — connect to Android devices in Developer Mode over your local Wi-Fi using ADB (Android Debug Bridge) for direct shell access and advanced troubleshooting.</item>
        <item>Built-in Viewers — view text files, PDFs, animated images (APNG, GIF, animated WebP, SVG and more), archives, and other formats directly within the app.</item>
        <item>Advanced ZIP Support — create and extract password-protected and AES-encrypted ZIP archives.</item>
        <item>Remote Screenshots — capture the screen of your paired Android TV over local Wi-Fi via ADB and save it directly to your phone\'s storage.</item>
        <item>7Z Archive Support — extract 7Z archives with LZMA/LZMA2 compression.</item>
        <item>File Search — quickly find files and folders across your device storage.</item>
        <item>Storage Analyser — see a visual breakdown of what\'s using your storage space.</item>
        <item>App Manager — view and manage all apps installed on your device, with debloat recommendations for pre-installed apps.</item>
        <item>APK Installer — install Android apps and split APKs (XAPK) directly from files saved locally.</item>
        <item>Elevated Access (Shizuku & ADB) — gain root-like access to manage system files and restricted directories without actually rooting your device.</item>
        <item>Storage Indexer — create a local index of file metadata for instant searching and blazing fast browsing.</item>
        <item>Storage Access Framework — other apps can access your files through UFM\'s document provider.</item>
        <item>Tip Jar — optional one-time purchases to support the developer; the app is always free without tipping.</item>

tc_risk_details.text:
<item>We cannot guarantee zero data loss. Always keep backups of files that matter to you.</item>
        <item>If you forget your PIN and Recovery Code, your encrypted files cannot be recovered — by anyone.</item>
        <item>Installing APKs from unknown sources carries security risks. You take full responsibility for any APK files you install.</item>
        <item>When hosting a File Server, FTP connections transmit data and credentials in plain text. Always use SFTP if you require secure, encrypted transfers.</item>
        <item>Your network share credentials (host, username, password) are stored locally on your device. You are responsible for keeping your device secure.</item>
        <item>Sync operations run in the background and may consume battery and data. Always verify your remote path before enabling sync — syncing to an incorrect folder may overwrite files on your network share.</item>
        <item>Removing system apps based on debloat recommendations may affect device stability. Proceed with caution.</item>
        <item>ADB pairing requires exchanging certificates between your device and the target device over your local Wi-Fi. Only connect to devices you own or have permission to access. Anyone on your network who captures your pairing PIN can access your device — keep this PIN private.</item>
        <item>Using Shizuku or ADB for elevated access allows the app to modify system-protected files. Misuse of these features could affect device stability or security. Use with caution and only grant access to this app.</item>
        <item>Screenshots of paired TVs are captured via ADB over your local network and saved directly to your phone\'s storage. We do not transmit, view, or upload your screenshots. Ensure you only capture screens on devices you own or have permission to access.</item>
        <item>The index reflects the state of your storage at the time of scanning. You may need to refresh the index if files are changed by other apps.</item>
        <item>No software is perfect. We can\'t promise the app will always be error-free or uninterrupted.</item>
        <item>Our total liability is capped at the total amount you paid for in-app purchases in the 30 days before any claim. We are not liable for data loss, device damage, or lost profits arising from free features.</item>

tc_responsibilities.text:
<item>Keep regular backups of important files before performing bulk operations.</item>
        <item>Store your Vault PIN and Recovery Code somewhere safe — we cannot retrieve them for you.</item>
        <item>Keep your PIN private. Anyone who knows it can access your Vault.</item>
        <item>Keep your network share credentials safe — they are stored locally on your device.</item>
        <item>Review your Folder Sync remote paths carefully — syncing to an incorrect network folder may overwrite existing files.</item>
        <item>Exercise caution when removing system apps based on debloat recommendations.</item>
        <item>Only connect via ADB Terminal to devices you own or have explicit permission to access. Do not use ADB Terminal to gain unauthorized access to any device.</item>
        <item>Keep any ADB or Shizuku pairing PINs private — share these only with people you trust to have access to your device.</item>
        <item>Secure your Shizuku Manager — granting UFM elevated access via Shizuku gives it power over restricted files. Only grant this access if you trust the app.</item>
        <item>Only use the app for lawful purposes. Don\'t store, share, or distribute illegal content.</item>
        <item>Don\'t use Remote Management to access another person\'s device without their permission.</item>
        <item>Don\'t attempt to reverse-engineer, decompile, or tamper with the app.</item>
        <item>Manage your indexed records responsibly — you can delete records or ignore specific drives at any time via Settings -> Storage Indexer.</item>
        <item>Verify the authenticity and safety of any APK files before installing them.</item>
